tagline: Korea's premier resort island — 13M+ visitors a year, UNESCO-listed coasts, and a mainland link still made on 4-hour diesel ferries.
summary: Jeju is Korea's holiday island: more than 15 million visitors in 2019 and consistently above 13 million a year since 2022, drawn to a UNESCO World Heritage volcanic landscape and a luxury-hotel coast (Shilla, Lotte, Grand Hyatt, Parnas). Yet the island's own scenic islets are reached by short, weather-exposed ferries, and the link to the mainland is a 4-to-5-hour diesel crossing of the Jeju Strait. A foiling network modernises a habit Jeju already has — moving people over the water — and makes both the islet-hopping and the mainland link smooth, fast and clean.

use_cases.title: Udo & Marado islet hops
use_cases.body: Short foiling shuttles from Seongsan to Udo (~2 nm) and from Moseulpo to Gapado/Marado replace crowded, weather-exposed excursion ferries to Jeju's signature islets — smooth, frequent and all-electric.

use_cases.title: Jungmun resort-coast arrivals
use_cases.body: Direct foiling transfers along the south coast to the Jungmun resort jetties (Shilla, Lotte, Grand Hyatt) turn an airport-plus-road transfer into one smooth water arrival for premium and inbound guests.

use_cases.title: Jeju ↔ mainland fast link
use_cases.body: An all-weather foiling crossing to Wando/Mokpo (~46–49 nm) and out to Busan (~150 nm) cuts the 4–5 hour diesel-ferry slog and adds reliability on a strait that regularly disrupts conventional sailings.

journeys.today: Queue for a packed diesel excursion ferry, weather-dependent, fixed timetable.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth ~2 nm all-electric hop, frequent and on-demand, landing at Udo with no pounding.

journeys.today: Drive to Jeju Port, then a 4-hour conventional ferry across the exposed strait.
journeys.with_navier: A fast, flat foiling crossing of the Jeju Strait — within all-electric range, with hybrid backup for all-weather reliability.

journeys.today: Long-haul ferry of many hours, or a flight; no fast, smooth sea option.
journeys.with_navier: A hybrid Quanta-LR line-haul (~150 nm) links the resort island directly to Korea's maritime capital with no charging dependency en route.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Runs the whole on-island and near-shore network: the Udo (~2 nm), Gapado/Marado, and Jungmun resort-coast hops, plus the nearest mainland crossings to Wando (~49 nm) and Mokpo (~46 nm), all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope (though the strait is exposed open water — see seasonality).
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Handles the long mainland line-haul — notably Jeju↔Busan (~150 nm) — and gives an all-weather, refuel-anywhere option on the longer or rougher strait crossings where charging-free range and sea-state margin matter most.

competitive_landscape: Jeju's water is moved today by conventional fast and car ferries to Mokpo, Wando and Busan (Hanil Express, Seaworld and others) and by diesel excursion boats to Udo, Gapado and Marado, while the resort coast relies on airport road transfers. The crossings are long, the islet ferries are weather-fragile, and none of it is clean or premium — an enormous, already-moving volume that a foiling network simply upgrades.
seasonality: Jeju sits under a dual weather overlay: the summer typhoon season (roughly Jul–Sep) and a strong winter NE monsoon that raises steep chop across the Jeju Strait and routinely delays or cancels ferries. Foiling above the surface is dramatically smoother and more reliable in exactly these windows, and the Quanta-LR hybrid adds range margin when conditions push crossings longer.
regulatory_note: Jeju is a Special Self-Governing Province with a lighter regulatory layer and the Jeju Free International City (JDC) economic-zone framework — a supportive environment for a clean-marine pilot. Operations sit under Korea's Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and Jeju Port authorities; the island's UNESCO World Heritage, Biosphere and Global Geopark designations make a zero-local-emission foiling fleet a natural fit for its conservation brand. Note the haenyeo (women divers) UNESCO living-heritage waters and protected coastal zones in route planning.
signature_routes: Jeju ↔ Wando / Mokpo mainland crossing (~46–49 nm)

sources.label: Jeju tourist numbers top 13M (Seoul Economic Daily)

precedents.why_it_matters: Proves a phased, island-wide clean-foiling network is commercially deliverable — the playbook to replicate for a high-volume resort island like Jeju.
